chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

The marriage of a female slave to a free woman is not valid, and the marriage of a free woman to a female slave is valid; so if he marries her, the division of nights is for the free woman two days and for the slave one day.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on dividing time between a free wife and a slave wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the hierarchical structure of polygyny within a single household, establishing that while a free man may marry both a free woman and his own slave, the free woman’s status takes precedence. It specifies a default equal division of time (two days for the free wife, one for the slave) unless otherwise agreed, reflecting the juristic principle of *tarjih* (preference) given to the higher social rank in marital rights. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the practical application of equity (*adl*) versus equality (*musawah*) in multi-wife households.
